{
 "map": true,
 "subject": {"columns": ["protein_id"], "resolver": "pharos_protein_gene", "category": "biolink:Gene"},
 "object": {"columns": ["trait"], "resolver": "pattern:OMIM:(\\d{6}) \\(\\d\\)\\s*$", "category": "biolink:Disease", "name_column": null},
 "predicate": "biolink:genetically_associated_with",
 "association_category": "biolink:GeneToDiseaseAssociation",
 "knowledge_level": "knowledge_assertion",
 "agent_type": "manual_agent",
 "primary_knowledge_source": "infores:omim",
 "qualifiers": {},
 "edge_properties": ["trait"],
 "keep_if": {"column": "trait", "matches": "Phenotype: .*\\b\\d{6} \\(\\d\\)\\s*$", "reason": "The leading MIM Number in trait is the gene's MIM number. A phenotype is asserted only when a 'Phenotype: name, MIM (key)' part is present and complete. Rows with only the gene MIM, or with a truncated phenotype, have no usable disease identifier."},
 "split_by": null,
 "notes": "In trait, 'MIM Number: N' is the gene's MIM (e.g. 114250 is CASQ1). The disease is the phenotype MIM before the '(mapping key)'. Subject is the protein's gene. The predicate is the generic genetic association, since the mapping key is not always causal. Trait strings cut off with '...' fail keep_if and become gaps.",
 "split_by_note": null
}
